If you could go back to the early days of the internet, would you handle privacy differently? Most people would. We should have been more careful about which services we used and what information we shared. Since time machines don't exist, we have to face reality. Your personal data is being bought and sold openly right now.

Your phone number, email address, home address, and even family relationships are now packaged and resold to marketing companies, insurance firms, and hackers. While Safari and Mail's built-in privacy features can block some tracking as you browse, they cannot erase information that has been collected over the years and scattered across hundreds of intermediary databases. Data brokers have built a multi-billion-dollar industry by collecting, packaging, and trading your digital information. It's time to take your personal data off the market and the internet. Let's look at how to do it together.

The security risks posed by data brokers

However, the danger goes far beyond annoying spam calls. When your information is easily accessible, you become an easy target for sophisticated cyberattacks. Since this industry is essentially unregulated, your most private information and details—including past employment, places you've lived, old loans, and more—can be purchased with ease, posing a significant threat to your safety.

Modern scammers use broker data to craft highly personalised and hard-to-spot phishing attacks. When scammers already know your job title, where you've lived, and even the names of your colleagues and friends, they can easily bypass your defensive instincts. Once a scammer knows everything about you, they only need to strike when your guard is down, dramatically increasing their chances of success.

For those concerned about personal safety, these websites and brokers function as a searchable public database, offering convenience to harassers and stalkers. By mapping out the relationship networks of your friends, family, and neighbours, brokers provide a tracking blueprint for individuals who deliberately keep a low profile and hide their whereabouts.

The solution: Incogni automated data removal service

This ecosystem is massive and frankly daunting. Submitting removal requests to hundreds of sites one by one is practically a full-time job—and the success rate is low—because if it were easy, these brokers would have gone out of business long ago. What you need is a solution that understands how this industry operates and sees through its various tactics, helping you regain control of your privacy rights.

That's exactly why services like Incogni have become essential to both your digital world and real life. This service transforms the major problem you face—your data being everywhere and traded—into a resolved one, offering a one-stop solution. You don't need to spend months tracking down data brokers one by one; Incogni automatically handles those repetitive and tedious opt-out procedures on your behalf. They ensure your data isn't just deleted once, but is continuously monitored and maintained, since brokers will inevitably attempt to re-collect it.

Incogni's comprehensive dashboard lets you track the progress of your personal data removal in real time, including:

  • The number of databases that may hold your information
  • Removal requests being issued on your behalf
  • Completed removal items and items still being followed up on

The real benefits of data removal for privacy-conscious individuals

Having your information removed from internet broker databases can deliver immediate results for you and your family.

  • When companies can't buy your number, scam calls and spam texts decrease.
  • Scammers lose their leads. Identity thieves typically obtain victim information from broker websites.
  • Your home address stays private, making it harder for stalkers and harassers to locate your residence.
  • Your credit score stays healthy, because less data exposure reduces the risk of identity theft and strengthens your overall financial health.
